How a Johnson County, IA DWI Attorney Can Protect Your Rights

Are you currently facing DWI charges in Johnson County? At Henkels & Baker, PC, we’re ready to help you along the way.

A DWI charge in Johnson County, Iowa, carries real consequences. First offenders might lose their driver’s license, face up to 2 years, or end up with a criminal record that follows them for years. The stakes are high from the moment of your arrest.

At Henkels & Baker, PC, we help people across Iowa respond to DWI charges. Our firm is based in Dubuque, IA, and we understand Iowa DWI law. We know what local courts look for and how to build a solid defense. Acting quickly can make a real difference in how your case moves forward. The sooner you have legal help, the more options may be available to you.

Remember, you have rights under Iowa law. We’re prepared to review every detail of your case to protect those rights.

How Henkels & Baker Approaches Your DWI Case in Johnson County

A DWI charge in Johnson County calls for a clear plan and speed. At Henkels & Baker, PC, we start by reviewing every detail of your case from the beginning. We look at how the traffic stop happened. Was it lawful? We check whether the officer followed proper steps.

Moreover, we can review any field sobriety tests or breathalyzer results. Errors in these areas can matter a great deal. Our team also looks at the evidence the state plans to use. Some evidence can be challenged. Some can be excluded.

Each case turns on its own facts, so we never take a one-size-fits-all approach.

We know what is at stake for you.

DWI Penalties in Johnson County, IA

A DWI in Johnson County, Texas, can lead to serious penalties. These may include jail time, large fines, and the loss of your driver’s license.

  • For a first offense, it is a Class B misdemeanor. You could face up to 180 days in jail and a fine of up to $2,000.

  • A second offense is a Class A misdemeanor. This can mean up to one year in jail and fines up to $4,000.

  • A third offense is a felony. You could get 2 to 10 years in prison and fines up to $10,000.

  • If a child under 15 is in the car, the charge may be a state jail felony. This can bring 180 days to 2 years in jail and fines up to $10,000.

  • More serious cases, like intoxication assault or manslaughter, carry even harsher penalties. Intoxication manslaughter can lead to 2 to 20 years in prison.

  • Your driver’s license can be suspended for up to two years. You may also have to pay additional state fines of $3,000 to $6,000, in addition to court fines.

A DWI can affect your life for years. You may have a permanent criminal record, higher insurance costs, and trouble finding a job or housing.

There are also automatic penalties. If you fail or refuse a breath or blood test, your license can be suspended right away. You may also need to install an ignition interlock device in your car before you can drive again.

Our goal is to protect as much of your normal life as possible.

When we identify weaknesses in the case, we advocate vigorously. We may seek a reduction in charges, a dismissal, or explore other options that fit your situation. If your case goes to court, we stand with you every step of the way.

Why Henkels & Baker, PC Stands Apart in DWI Defense

Henkels & Baker, PC brings a focused, client-centered approach to DWI defense in Johnson County.

Here is what sets us apart.

DWI/OWI Defense as a Core Focus

Henkels & Baker, PC keeps its practice focused. We handle DWI/OWI defense and debt relief — not a broad mix of unrelated legal matters. That focus means we know DWI law well. You get real attention on your case, not a rushed file in a crowded caseload.

Serving a Wide Region Around Eastern Iowa

Our firm serves clients across a wide area — roughly 100 miles around our Dubuque, IA base. That includes clients from Johnson County and surrounding areas. If you are facing DWI charges in Iowa, we are close by and ready to help.

A Small Office That Treats You Like a Person

Henkels & Baker, PC is a small, friendly firm. You will not get lost in a big office. You will know your attorney. You will get direct answers. Clients tell us they feel supported from the very first call, and that matters when the stakes are high.

A Track Record Clients Can Count On

We work diligently to help clients protect their assets in our debt relief work. That same care and thoroughness carries into every DWI case we take on. We protect what matters most: your license, your job, and your future.

Your DWI Case in Johnson County: What Happens Next

A DWI charge in Johnson County moves through the Iowa District Court for Johnson County in Iowa City. The process has several stages. Knowing what each one looks like can help you stay calm and make smart choices.

Stage 1: Arrest and Booking

After an arrest, you are booked and may be held briefly before release. The arresting officer files a report. You have just 10 days to request a hearing with the Iowa Department of Transportation to challenge your administrative license revocation.

Miss that window, and your license is suspended by default.

Stage 2: Initial Appearance and Arraignment  

Your first court date happens quickly — often within a few days of arrest. The judge reads the charges. You enter a plea. At this stage, your attorney reviews the arrest report, the implied consent notice, and any breath or blood test results for errors or rights violations.

Stage 3: Pre-Trial Review and Motions  

This is where the most important legal work happens. Your attorney can file motions to suppress evidence if the traffic stop or arrest was not lawful under Iowa law. The prosecutor may offer a plea deal.

Both sides trade discovery materials. Johnson County cases often resolve during this stage.

Stage 4: Plea or Trial

If no deal is reached, the case goes to trial in Iowa City. A jury or judge decides the outcome. As your attorney, we are ready to cross-examine witnesses and challenge the state’s evidence.

Stage 5: Sentencing and Afterward

A first-offense DWI in Iowa can mean fines, license suspension, and possible jail time under Iowa Code § 321J.2. We are prepared to argue for reduced penalties, a deferred judgment, or alternative sentencing.

After sentencing, steps like substance abuse evaluation and ignition interlock installation may follow.

Talk to a Johnson County, IA DWI Attorney Today

A DWI charge in Johnson County moves fast. The sooner you act, the more options you may have to protect your license and your future. At Henkels & Baker, PC, we offer free consultations. There’s no pressure and no obligation. Just a plain conversation about your situation and what your next steps might look like.

Contact us today to get started. Don’t wait. A DWI case has deadlines, and early action matters.  

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Can I still drive after a DWI arrest in Iowa?

Your license may be suspended right away after a DWI arrest in Iowa. You have 10 days to request a hearing with the Iowa DOT to fight that suspension. Missing that window can cost you your license for months.

2. What if I refused the breath test during my traffic stop?

Iowa’s implied consent law means refusing a breath test carries its own penalties, including an automatic one-year license revocation. A Johnson County, IA DWI attorney can review whether the officer followed proper implied consent procedures before the penalty sticks.

3. Will a DWI conviction show up on my permanent record in Iowa?

In Iowa, a DWI conviction stays on your criminal record and is visible in background checks for jobs, housing, and licensing. Deferred judgment may be an option in some cases, leading to dismissal after probation. We can determine if you qualify.

4. What happens if this is my second DWI in Iowa?

A second DWI in Iowa is treated as an aggravated misdemeanor, which carries harsher fines, longer license loss, and possible jail time. The stakes rise sharply, so having a Johnson County, IA DWI attorney review the prior conviction and current charges is critical.
